Monitor the water temperature (26–28 °C) with an alcohol thermometer placed upstream of the pump or with a temperature sensor. If, after multiple trials, the embryo medium moves above 28 °C, then place a small freezer pack just before the pump inlet (see Troubleshooting section) or replace the overheated media with fresh media.

steps.title: Print and assemble microflume
steps.instruction: Download STL files from the GitHub or OSF repository, edit in Fusion 360 if needed, export to PreForm, auto‑orient and add supports, then print with FormLabs Clear V5 resin on a medium‑format resin printer. De‑support parts with flush cutters, micro‑pliers and forceps, hand‑tap screw holes (M2 ×0.5 mm pitch), and wash all parts repeatedly with 70‑99 % ethanol. For printers with a small build volume, split the body into two pieces, add three 3 mm alignment pins, coat junctions with resin, press together and wipe excess resin. Cure the printed parts in a FormLabs curing chamber. Laser‑cut a 1.5 mm 3M 9448A silicone/rubber gasket and a 3 mm clear acrylic top plate, wash the gasket with warm soapy water and dry. Place the gasket between the microflume body and acrylic plate, secure with M2 × 8 mm screws. Install the thruster motor (pump) in the flume, glue with Loctite super glue and clear silicone sealant, and connect to an Arduino controller. Cut 3 mm polypropylene straws to 40 mm, bind with nylon mesh and Loctite, and position upstream of the fish basket. Assemble a removable fish basket (30 × 30 × 10 mm) by cutting nylon mesh for the bottom and sides and adhering with Loctite.

steps.title: Prepare 1× E3 medium
steps.instruction: Dilute 16.7 mL of 60× E3 stock into 1 L of reverse‑osmosis or deionized water to obtain a 1× working solution containing 5 mM NaCl, 0.17 mM KCl, 0.33 mM CaCl₂·2H₂O, and 0.33 mM MgSO₄·7H₂O.

steps.title: Prepare 1× embryo medium
steps.instruction: Make a 1 L working solution by adding to reverse‑osmosis or deionized water: 15 mL of 1 M NaCl (15 mM final), 500 µL of 1 M KCl (0.5 mM), 1 mL of 1 M CaCl₂ (1 mM), 1 mL of 1 M MgSO₄·7H₂O (1 mM), 150 µL of 1 M KH₂PO₄ (0.15 mM), 42 µL of 1 M Na₂HPO₄ (0.042 mM), and 714 µL of 1 M NaHCO₃ (0.714 mM).

steps.title: Set up rheotaxis rig
steps.instruction: If this is the first run, assemble the rig as shown in Figure 2, connect the Arduino to the PC via USB and install the Arduino IDE. Pre‑warm 1 L of embryo medium (E3 or EM) to 27 °C in an incubator, rinse the flume and fish basket with distilled water, turn on the PC and plug in camera, IR light, Arduino and control boxes, and set the potentiometer to approximately 130–135. Place the light diffuser between the flume and light source.

steps.title: Fill flume and remove bubbles
steps.instruction: Fill the flume with distilled water, then use a glass or plastic pipette to remove all bubbles from the fish basket, basket grooves, and straws; any remaining bubbles will alter flow rate and may be misidentified by DeepLabCut.

steps.title: Configure camera and test system
steps.instruction: Connect the camera, check the live feed, and center the arena with ~20 px border for later cropping. For an Edgertronic camera, connect power, Ethernet, and trigger to the Arduino, insert the SD card, wait for steady green and yellow LEDs, then open Chrome at 10.11.12.13 and the storage page to monitor files. Adjust focus by placing a 3–5 mm screw in the basket and focusing on it. Set camera exposure for high larval contrast at 60 fps (Edgertronic: ISO 20000, 1/1000 s shutter, f/16, 40 s duration). Perform test runs without fish, pressing SELECT on the Arduino for the first run and DOWN thereafter, and verify that video is recorded, the pump starts and stops, and a video file is generated.

steps.title: Run behavior trial with fish
steps.instruction: Replace the distilled water with pre‑warmed 26–28 °C embryo medium, remove any bubbles or lint with a transfer pipette, turn on the IR light and verify the live feed, and monitor water temperature upstream of the pump with an alcohol thermometer or sensor; if temperature exceeds 28 °C, place a small freezer pack before the pump inlet or replace the media. Turn off overhead lights or work in a dark box, using an LED flashlight and setting PC monitor brightness to 0. Transfer a single, actively swimming larva into the basket with a transfer pipette, discarding fish that are not swimming or appear sick and removing any debris. Press SELECT/DOWN on the Arduino to start recording (10 s no flow, 20 s flow, 10 s no flow) using the timing parameters int Initime = 2, CamTrigTime = 1, pumpDelay = 10, pumpOnsec = 20. After recording, remove the fish and place it in a labeled well of a 24‑well plate containing pre‑warmed embryo medium for later genotyping or histology, noting the video file name and well location. Insert a new fish and repeat the procedure, avoiding long idle periods that could bias the pre‑stimulus data. Keep track of the number of fish per condition, adjust filenames when switching conditions, and turn off the IR light when pausing to prevent media overheating.

steps.title: Post‑experiment data handling
steps.instruction: After all trials, store raw video files in a clearly named folder on the computer for downstream analysis, then turn off all rheotaxis equipment and verify that the infrared light is off to avoid overheating.
